surfaces.part: side body with windows and doors
slanted windshield at the left (front) end

answer.evidence: The van is drawn in side view facing left. Its roof is a wide yellow band at rows 6-16, about 10 rows tall, with a highlight pattern at rows 7-13. The band ends in a darker edge line at row 16, and rows 17-18 add a dark eave and window-frame shadow. Below that sits a side face of about 25 rows (rows 17-41) with windows, door seams, a lower body and wheels. The roof therefore reads as a foreshortened top surface above the south-facing side, not a rim. No isometric receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate van has a yellow body ramp of about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark) plus a blue-grey window ramp. The references use 5-6 steps per material. 88% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line around the whole shape with little tinting toward the adjacent yellow or glass. That is the sticker look, unlike the tinted outlines on the hedge (0%) and the cheese stall (1%). Visible tones per tile are 9, equal to the hedge but well below the well (20) and the stall (17). Flat coverage is 15%, slightly above the stall's 13% and the references' 0%. The body panels, roof and window are fairly smooth fills with only a few highlight streaks and no grain, speckle or per-part material texture. Overall it is cleanly drawn but shallower and flatter than the best references.
